newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk coalition conservative say polls this year.
newsitem.headline: Turk coalition conservative say polls this year.

text.p: The Turkish government's conservative coalition partners said on Monday early elections would be held by the end of the year under a deal with Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
"This election will be carried out by the end of 1997," Hasan Ekinci, deputy chairman of the True Path Party, told a news conference.
Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist leader, announced on Sunday he would step down in favour of True Path leader Tansu Ciller within a month.
He said Foreign Minister Ciller would then head a caretaker government to go to elections, but set no date.
Pressure from the generals to carry out an anti-Islamist crackdown brought the 11-month-old coalition to breaking point.

Turkish newspapers said on Monday that President Suleyman Demirel, who would have a key role in any power handover, may throw a spanner in the works of the planned transition by saying their is no clear formula for giving the office of prime minister to a coalition partner.
